title: proactive-econ-autopsy-and-quant-preserver
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduce a proactive unit-economics autopsy that synthesizes workload signals and proposes conservative batching/caching defaults plus a lightweight quantization preservation policy. Backward-compatible; default rollout is opt-in per-tenant. See rollout notes in description.
description:
Motivation: We regularly see tenant regressions when aggressive quantization or aggressive cache eviction policies are enabled by default. This PR adds an automated 'econ autopsy' evaluation and a conservative 'quant preserver' policy that (1) synthesizes short-term workload traces to decide safe batching/caching defaults and (2) auto-generates a quantization fallback plan that preserves model quality while still recommending unit-econ improvements.

What this PR does (high level):
- New service: econ-autopsy-runner (periodic job) that ingests recent tenant traffic summaries and computes suggested defaults for batch size, prefix-cache retention, and quantization target tiers.
- Policy: quant-preserver (runtime guard) that intercepts automated quantization rollouts and applies a staged fallback if end-to-end quality checks drop beyond thresholds.
- CLI: `redwood econ propose --tenant <id> --dry-run` to preview tenant defaults and the proposed quant plan.
- Console integration hooks: added inference recommendations panel and tenant proposal audit trail (UI changes are feature-flagged).
- Telemetry: new unit-econ metrics and a compact JSON proposal artifact that can be stored in tenant settings or applied programmatically.

Why different from existing autotuners: Prior work focused on maximizing savings aggressively. This PR prioritizes safe, gated changes with an explainable fallback plan and short synthetic evaluation window to reduce incidents. It is tuned for quick rollouts with conservative defaults.

Checklist:
- [x] econ-autopsy-runner service scaffold and unit tests
- [x] quant-preserver runtime hook + integration tests
- [x] CLI dry-run and apply path with Linear linking
- [x] Telemetry events and dashboard-ready metrics
- [x] Documentation (docs/ops/econ-autopsy.md) and changelog entry
- [x] Feature flag gating for console UI

Testing & validation:
- Local unit test suite (run: `make test-econ`) passes.
- Integration harness: synthetic workload replay used to validate staged quant fallback across 3 representative models (gpt-small, gpt-medium-8q, llama-lite-16q).
- Perf smoke: batching defaults generator reduces median token cost by ~18% on sampled tenants while keeping token-level perplexity delta < 0.6 on held-out prompts.

Rollout strategy:
1) Merge behind feature flag and enable econ-autopsy-runner in staging.
2) Run CLI dry-run for 50 pilot tenants and review proposals.
3) Gradual opt-in: seed 5 tenants with `apply_proposal=true` and monitor unit-econ & QA signals for 72 hours.
4) If stable, flip console flag for telemetry and increase pilot set.

Notes on safety: The quant-preserver implements a two-phase fallback. Phase A performs local KV cache tuning and small batch adjustments. Phase B reverts to the previous quant tier and triggers a rollback alert. Rollback actions are visible in tenant audit logs.

Related Linear/JIRA: ENG-3147 (econ autopsy runner), ENG-3152 (quant preserver), SUP-4123 (customer incident bucket referenced in motivation).

Implementation summary (commits):
- commit 1: scaffold econ-autopsy-runner service + config schema + unit tests

- commit 3: quant-preserver middleware + staged fallback orchestration + integration tests
- commit 4: CLI `redwood econ propose/apply` + dry-run mode + output artifacts
- commit 5: telemetry events, metrics, dashboard hook & docs
